subject: Clarify: 'last processing moment' vs event timestamp for SOC 2 coverage
messages:
From: compliance@fintechco.com
To: lukas.meyer@redwood.ai
Cc: audit@auditsrus.com
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Clarify: last processing moment included in SOC 2 period

Hi Lukas,

We are preparing evidence for our SOC 2 Type II assessment and need to confirm Redwood's interpretation of the audit coverage. The assessor is asking whether 'last processing moment' is defined by: (A) the event timestamp attached to a transaction record (user event time), or (B) the time the record was processed/safe-stored by your system (processing time).

Example scenario: a credit auth request arrives at 23:58 (event timestamp 2026-11-30T23:58:12Z) but is processed by your backend at 00:03 on 2026-12-01 (processing time). For the November 2026 SOC 2 window, does Redwood treat that record as in-scope for November (based on event timestamp) or December (based on processing time)?

Please confirm which timestamp your submitted logs and manifest use as the authoritative inclusion boundary, and whether you can provide a short manifest tying example transaction IDs to both timestamps. Our auditor also asked about any backfill or replay jobs that could alter the original processing times.

Thanks,
Rita Chen
Compliance Manager
FintechCo

---

From: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.ai>
To: compliance@fintechco.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, audit@auditsrus.com
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 11:07:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Clarify: last processing moment included in SOC 2 period

Hi Rita,

Thanks for the clear example — that helps. Short answer: our standard evidence manifests for SOC 2 Type II are keyed to 'processing time' (the moment the record was durably written to our production datastore), not the user-provided event timestamp. That is because our control tests (access, encryption-at-rest, retention) operate on persisted records.

That said, we can provide a crosswalk manifest showing both fields for a sample set of transaction IDs (event_timestamp, processing_timestamp). I attached a provisional log_manifest_2026-11.csv with a small sample and a draft bridge_letter_draft.docx that explains our interpretation for auditors.

A few important caveats:
- If you run any replay/backfill that writes historical events into production after the audit cutoff, those writes will be treated as new processing events (and therefore fall after the cutoff).
- We also capture an ingestion_agent marker: if an ingest service accepted the event but placed it in a queue (and the queue flush occurred before cutoff), processing_time reflects the durable write, not the queue accept.

Marissa (CC'd) — can you confirm there were no scheduled backfills impacting FintechCo in the November window? Karthik, are there any infra exceptions (lagging replicas/backfills) we should call out in the bridge letter?

Best,
Lukas
Senior Compliance Ops
Redwood Inference

Attachment: log_manifest_2026-11.csv (sample mapping transaction_id,event_timestamp,processing_timestamp)

---

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: lukas.meyer@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, compliance@fintechco.com, audit@auditsrus.com
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 08:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Clarify: last processing moment included in SOC 2 period

Lukas — quick operational confirmation: no customer-facing backfills for FintechCo occurred between 2026-11-25 and 2026-12-02. We did have an internal log-retention prune on 2026-11-29 that is read-only and does not rewrite historical events.

Karthik — the engineering note about queue vs durable write is important; can we add a one-paragraph note to the bridge letter that lists: 1) our definition (processing_time = durable write to primary datastore), 2) exceptions (explicit backfill jobs, admin replays), and 3) a short list of systems that could produce delayed processing (ingest-queue, replica catchup). I'll pull a short vetted sentence for the draft.

Marissa
Director, Trust & Security
Redwood Inference

Attachment: none (but planning update to bridge_letter_draft.docx)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, lukas.meyer@redwood.ai, compliance@fintechco.com
Cc: audit@auditsrus.com
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 15:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Clarify: last processing moment included in SOC 2 period

Rita / FintechCo team — adding a technical note for auditors:

1) Processing timestamp definition: processing_timestamp = time_uuid assigned on successful commit to the primary partitioner (UTC).
2) Queueing behavior: events that are accepted into the ingest queue but not yet committed will have processing_timestamp when the commit occurs; if that commit happens after the audit cutoff, those records are out-of-scope for the earlier period.
3) Replays/backfills: we keep separate evidence of administrative replay jobs; those jobs create new processing entries and are therefore scoped to their processing time. We can include an appendix in the bridge letter enumerating replay job IDs and windows.

I've attached the draft bridge letter paragraph and the small CSV sample (transaction ids 7 shown) to help your assessor follow the logic. If you want, we can also produce a signed statement confirming no targeted backfills occurred for the window.

Let me know if the auditor needs the crosswalk as a CSV with checksums.

Karthik
Staff Site Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment: bridge_letter_draft.docx (proposed paragraph + appendix), log_manifest_2026-11.csv (sample)
